decisions.reason: After several years without website evidence, this bread's prospects look largely learned and likely modest, so its low but nonzero carrying cost no longer justifies keeping the option open.
The guided mill tour requires staff and organizational effort, and two years without visibility make its demand look too uncertain relative to its higher holding cost.
A sweet pastry is easy to test within the core range, but the lack of later evidence suggests weak standalone traction, so the option value now appears limited.
As a recent farmhouse bread close to the firm's craft core, it is inexpensive to continue and the disrupted recent period means there is still enough uncertainty to justify waiting longer.

The poppy seed Christmas stollen is a flagged strategic product with award-based positive evidence and strong fit with the firm's seasonal specialty capabilities, so it remains an attractive option to retain.

The premium Christmas stollen also has positive quality signaling from its gold award and can be produced within existing seasonal routines, though overlap with other stollen lines gives it somewhat higher exit risk than E.
